# `Alert`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Fault notification, in one of two shapes (code/error, or Msg/Type), including the connection-limit rejection.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | event (device sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, SendAlert @0x125d60, common_netThd @0x6b7430; guider SendAlert @0x6d9a0, NotifyAlert @0x6e290, CheckMoveLimit @0x6dc60, get_err_string table @0x1f24b0, imager CTrackStateChecker::handleTrackState @0x186d10 (64-bit builds) |

Emitted for operational faults, connection-limit rejection and guider/UI alerts; no universal throttle. Emitted by the imager on TCP 4700 (channel I) and by the guider on TCP 4400 (channel G); guider event lines are forwarded onto 4700 by the imager main process. Ordinary alerts go to all retained sockets. Two payload forms exist and must not be merged into one mandatory shape: (1) the fault form from the alert sender, code plus error (message from the shared error-code table), optionally wide_cam (imager camera origin) or required_storage_mb (storage-required fault); (2) the Msg/Type form used by the common server rejection and by guider UI alerts, where the guider maps severity to Type info, error, warning or question. The guider also uses the fault form: during a scope_speed_move its movement-limit worker emits code 532 (move upper limit), 533 (move lower limit), 540 or 541 (both rendered fail to operate, because the guider error table has no text for them), after asking the imager to play a warning sound; it repeats about every 3 s while the limit persists. A client SHOULD stop the move on one of these. The imager raises the fault form from a forwarded ScopeTrack off event that is not a manual transition and carries code 270 (below horizon) or 527 (alt exceed limit), with wide_cam; this is how a mount dropping below the horizon surfaces as an Alert during a view or live stack. Connection-limit variant (common server): after accepting a socket, the server rejects it when its count of distinct external source addresses exceeds 2 (guest mode off) or 8 (guest mode on); unverified external sockets count, local internal sockets do not, and other servers are not summed. Only the rejected socket receives Event Alert with code 429, Type error and Msg "Exceed the maximum number of connections", then the socket is closed before normal arrival handling (so no Version greeting). Delivery is attempted, not guaranteed; it is an event followed by EOF, not an RPC error. The code list is not closed: a code in the shared table is not proof that Alert emits it. APK consumers: the app event dispatcher (alert payload), the app device service, the app connection service.

Side effects: Observation only. The connection-limit form is followed by the device closing that socket.

## Request params

None. Events are sent by the device without a request; the payload is below.

## Payload

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Event` | string | yes | - | Discriminator. Fixed value `"Alert"`. [READ] |
| `Timestamp` | string | yes | - | Decimal string with nine fractional digits from a monotonic clock; not a calendar time. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | if fault form; connection-limit form (429) | - | Fault code, or 429 on the connection-limit form. Guider speed-move limit alerts use 532, 533, 540 or 541. The imager track-state alert uses 270 (below horizon) or 527 (alt exceed limit). [READ] |
| `error` | string | if fault form (alert sender) | - | Message looked up for code. Not part of the Msg/Type form. A code with no table entry (guider 540, 541) falls back to fail to operate. [READ] |
| `wide_cam` | boolean | if when the imager producer includes it | - | Imager camera-origin flag. [READ] |
| `required_storage_mb` | integer | if storage-required fault branch | - | Storage required, megabytes (unit from the member name). [READ; unit INFERRED] |
| `Msg` | string | if Msg/Type form (server rejection, guider UI alert) | - | Alert text; on the connection-limit form the literal Exceed the maximum number of connections. [READ] |
| `Type` | string | if Msg/Type form | - | Severity. error on the connection-limit form; the guider maps severity to info, error, warning or question. [READ] |

## Errors

None. Failures appear in the payload (`code`, `error`) when `state` is `fail`.

## Example

Event, connection-limit - Rejected-socket form (READ literals, not captured):

```json
{"Event":"Alert","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","code":429,"Type":"error","Msg":"Exceed the maximum number of connections"}
```

Event, fault - Fault form (READ shape; code and message invented):

```json
{"Event":"Alert","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","code":999,"error":"example error message","wide_cam":false}
```

Event, speed-move-limit - Guider limit alert during a speed move (READ shape and code text):

```json
{"Event":"Alert","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","code":532,"error":"move upper limit"}
```

Event, track-below-horizon - Imager alert when the mount drops below the horizon (READ shape and code):

```json
{"Event":"Alert","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","code":270,"error":"below horizon","wide_cam":false}
```
